title: Internship Interview Questions (2027): 15 Common Ones and How to Answer
summary: How to prepare, sample replies for behavioral and technical rounds, what to ask at the end, and how long Simplify users waited to hear back after applying.
body_markdown:
Most internship interviews use the same fifteen or so questions in different words: a few about you, a few behavioral questions about things you have done, and one or two about the field. Prepare a short answer for each of the fifteen below, practice them out loud, and bring two questions of your own for the end.


The questions are predictable. The part candidates underestimate is how fast the interview comes. On Simplify, the typical wait from applying to a first screen was under two weeks (more on that below), so prepare before you apply, not after the recruiter emails.


## The 15 questions at a glance


# Question What they want to know


1 **Tell me about yourself.** Can you summarize yourself in a minute?


2 **Why do you want this internship?** Did you pick us on purpose?


3 **Why our company?** Do you know what we do?


4 **What do you know about this team or role?** Did you prepare?


5 **What are your career goals?** Does this internship fit your plan?


6 **Tell me about a time you worked on a team.** How you collaborate


7 **Tell me about a challenge you faced.** How you handle problems


8 **Tell me about a time you disagreed with someone.** How you handle conflict


9 **Tell me about a time you learned something quickly.** How fast you ramp up


10 **What project are you most proud of?** What you can actually do


11 **What are your strengths?** Self-awareness, with proof


12 **What is a weakness you are working on?** Honesty and growth


13 **How will you balance this with classes?** Reliability


14 **A technical or field question** The basic skills for the role


15 **Do you have any questions for us?** Curiosity and preparation


## Questions about you


### 1. Tell me about yourself


Answer in about a minute, in three parts: what you study now, one or two experiences that led you here, and why you are interested in this internship. Do not walk through your whole resume. The interviewer already has it.


> "I'm a sophomore studying computer science. Last summer I built a scheduling tool for my school's tutoring center that about 300 students now use, and it made me want to work on products with real users. That's why I applied to your consumer apps team." (Made-up example.)


### 2. Why do you want this internship?


Use three parts: what you want to learn, why this company and not another, and what you bring. Name one specific detail about the company. We wrote a full guide with examples for tech, finance and consulting:[how to answer "Why do you want this internship?"](https://simplify.jobs/blog/why-do-you-want-this-internship?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) .


### 3. Why our company?


Similar to question 2, but about the company rather than the role. Mention a product you use, a recent announcement, or something an employee told you. One real detail beats three general compliments.


### 4. What do you know about this team or role?


Read the job description twice and the team's public pages once. Be able to say in one or two sentences what the team works on and what an intern on it would do. If you are not sure, say what you found and ask them to fill in the rest.


### 5. What are your career goals?


You do not need a ten-year plan. Name the kind of work you want to explore and show how this internship fits. "I want to find out whether I like product work or engineering work more, and this role touches both" is a good answer.


## Behavioral questions


For these five, use the STAR structure: the situation, your task, the action you took and the result. Keep the situation short and spend most of the time on what you did. Our[behavioral interview guide](https://simplify.jobs/blog/prepare-behavioral-interview-without-sounding-rehearsed?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) has more examples.


### 6. Tell me about a time you worked on a team


Pick a group project, club, team sport or job where you had a clear role. Say what you were responsible for and how the team decided things, not only what the team achieved.


### 7. Tell me about a challenge you faced


Choose a real problem you solved, not a story where everything went right. End with what you would do differently next time.


### 8. Tell me about a time you disagreed with someone


Show that you listened, explained your view with reasons, and moved forward. Avoid stories where the other person was simply wrong.


### 9. Tell me about a time you learned something quickly


Interns spend the first weeks learning. Describe a tool, subject or job you picked up fast and how you did it: what you read, who you asked, what you practiced.


### 10. What project are you most proud of?


Pick the project you can talk about in the most detail, and lead with the result. If it is on your resume, the bullet should already say what you did and how it was measured, as in the[XYZ resume format](https://simplify.jobs/blog/how-to-use-the-xyz-resume-format?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) .


## Skills and fit


### 11. What are your strengths?


Name two, each with a short example. "I'm organized" means little; "I ran our club's 40-person event schedule for a year without a missed booking" shows it.


### 12. What is a weakness you are working on?


Pick a real one that will not stop you doing the job, and say what you are doing about it. "I used to wait too long to ask for help, so now I give myself an hour before I ask" works. "I'm a perfectionist" does not.


### 13. How will you balance this with classes?


This comes up for part-time and semester internships. Give your actual schedule and how many hours you can commit, and mention a time you balanced work and school before.


### 14. A technical or field question


What comes up depends on the role:


Field What to expect Where to prepare


Software engineering A coding problem, often easy to medium Our[Amazon](https://simplify.jobs/blog/amazon-swe-interview-new-grads?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) and[Google](https://simplify.jobs/blog/google-new-grad-swe-interview-guide?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) interview guides


Finance Accounting basics, a walk-through of a DCF, a recent deal Our[finance early insight programs](https://simplify.jobs/blog/list-of-finance-early-insight-programs-for-underclassmen?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) guide


Consulting A short case: sizing a market or diagnosing a problem Our[consulting insight programs](https://simplify.jobs/blog/list-of-consulting-insight-programs-for-underclassmen?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) guide


Design A portfolio walk-through Two projects you can explain from problem to result


Marketing or operations How you would approach a real task, like launching a campaign One example from a class, club or job


If you do not know an answer, say how you would figure it out. Interviewers often care more about how you think than whether you get it right.


### 15. Do you have any questions for us?


Always have two ready. Good ones:


- "What does a typical week look like for an intern on this team?"
- "What did last year's interns work on?"
- "How will my work be reviewed, and by whom?"
- "What do you like most about working here?"
- "What are the next steps, and when should I expect to hear back?"


Skip questions the job description already answers, and save pay and benefits for after an offer unless they ask you first.


## How long until the interview? What we see on Simplify


We looked at internship applications in Simplify's Job Tracker that moved from Applied to a first screen or interview between August and October 2026. Among the 3,440 where the screen came at least a day after the application, the median wait was **12 days** . A quarter heard back within **5 days** , and three quarters within about **25 days** .


Two caveats. These are applications people chose to track and update, so they are not every application on Simplify, and the dates are when the status was recorded, which can lag the actual email. We also left out same-day updates, which are often entered after the fact. Read the numbers as a rough guide.


What it means for you: if you apply in the fall, a first-round call can come within a week or two. Prepare your answers to questions 1, 2 and 10 before you start applying.


## A one-week prep plan


When What to do


Before you apply Write answers to questions 1, 2 and 10. Update your resume.


Interview scheduled Research the company and team. Prepare questions 3, 4 and 15.


3 days before Practice behavioral answers (6 to 9) out loud, ideally with a friend.


1 day before Review the job description, test your video setup, plan your outfit.


After the interview Send a short thank-you note within 24 hours.


## Common questions


**How do I prepare for an internship interview?** Prepare short answers to the 15 common questions above, research the company and team, practice out loud, and bring two questions to ask. Most of the work is the same for every company; only questions 2 to 4 change.


**How long does it take to hear back from an internship after applying?** It varies by company. Among internship applications Simplify users tracked to a first screen or interview from August to October 2026, the median wait was 12 days, and three quarters heard back within about 25 days.


**How long is an internship interview?** First-round calls are usually 20 to 30 minutes. Later rounds are often 45 to 60 minutes each, and some companies hold several back to back.


**What should I wear to an internship interview?** One step more formal than what people wear at the company day to day. For video interviews, a plain top and a quiet background are enough.


**What should I ask at the end of an internship interview?** Ask about what interns actually work on, how they are supported and what the next steps are. Two good questions are enough.


## After the interview


Move the application to Interviewing in Simplify's free[Job Tracker](https://simplify.jobs/job-application-tracker?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=most-common-internship-interview-questions-to-prep-for&utm_content=after-interview) and add a note with the interviewer's name and what you talked about, so your thank-you note and any later round can build on it. With[Simplify+](https://simplify.jobs/plus?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=most-common-internship-interview-questions-to-prep-for&utm_content=thank-you) , AI Email drafts that thank-you note from the job you tracked, and you edit and send it yourself.


Simplify is used by more than 2 million job seekers. In a 2022 survey of Harvard CS students it ranked among the top three places they found tech internships ([Harvard career center, archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20240228134502/https://careerservices.fas.harvard.edu/blog/2022/11/22/beyond-big-tech-where-can-i-find-summer-opportunities/) ), and the University of Washington's career center[recommends it](https://careers.uw.edu/resources/simplify/?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) for applying faster.
